text.p: Weakness in fine paper prices was the biggest single reason behind a profit warning from Metsa-Serla Oy on Tuesday, a senior Metsa-Serla official said.

The company said in a statement that price weakness in pulp and paper products would mean losses in May-December, but on the back of a 318 million markka profit after financial items in January-April, the full-year should still be in the black.
"The biggest impact is indeed from fine paper prices," Metsa-Serla senior vice president Hannu Anttila told Reuters in a telephone interview after the profit-warning. @
"The turn has happened but it came at such a low level ... prices are still very unsatisfactory," Anttila said, meaning fine paper prices had turned higher.
But he declined to say whether Metsa-Serla was still making losses at the current fine paper price levels.
"The low level of the bottom price was really a surprise," he said. @

Magazine paper prices were also weaker than expected and the no upturn had emerged there yet, but they did not have as big a detrimentary impact on Metsa-Serla's outlook as weak pulp and fine paper prices, he said.
"The upturn in magazine papers has been delayed," he said.
